annotationRationale: Tangent-radius perpendicularity and equal radii determine the centers. Coordinates provide the main calculation; the alternative uses their shared perpendicular bisector and similar triangles.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area recommendation is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, coordinates C=(0,0), B=(6,0), A=(0,8) give O=(6,25/4) and P=(25/3,8). Their distance is 35/12, choice C. The stem and key agree; no question figure or contradictory geometric condition is supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. The LIVE and AoPS Solution 3 coordinate route is retained. AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 are retained through the perpendicular-bisector and similarity method. Solutions 4 and 5 combine the same center locus, similarity or coordinate calculations and do not warrant another route.
review.annotationCheck: Tangent-radius perpendicularity is correctly assessed, with equal radii as support. Coordinate distance and perpendicular-bisector similarity are appropriately method-local.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area recommendation is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The tangent conditions correctly fix O=(6,k) and P=(h,8). Equal-radius equations reduce to 100-16k=0 and 100-12h=0. The resulting coordinate differences 7/3 and 7/4 give OP=35/12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The route matches the cited LIVE explanation and AoPS Solution 3. The candidate uses consistent coordinates throughout, avoiding the coordinate inconsistencies in the archived AoPS transcription. The prose is independently explanatory and the third-party designation is correct.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The coordinate choice is motivated by the tangent conditions. Both center equations and the final distance calculation are shown sufficiently for reconstruction.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_262 supplies tangent-radius perpendicularity, cnm_p188 supplies equal radii, and cnm_h173 supplies every distance equation. A circle-equation node is unnecessary because no circle equation is used.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All three nodes have accepted exact native-topic links and are directly exercised.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-C.A.2 contributes its tangent-radius component. The accepted exact 8.G.B.8 link fits coordinate distance; the broader polygon perimeter and area work in the partial G-GPE.B.7 link is not exercised.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The three immediate nodes precisely cover the geometric setup and coordinate calculation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Equal distances place both centers on the perpendicular bisector of AB. Tangency selects the same perpendicular ray from M. The stated AA correspondences give MO=15/4 and MP=20/3, so their difference is 35/12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The shared perpendicular bisector and the two similar-triangle calculations are present in AoPS Solutions 1 and 2. The candidate adds its own explanation of center placement and subtraction, with accurate nonofficial source credit.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The center locus motivates the construction. Parallel-line angles establish both similarities explicitly, and the same-ray explanation justifies subtracting rather than adding the distances. The words suffice without a new diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five IDs are directly used: tangent perpendicularity, equal radii, the equidistance locus, AA similarity and proportional corresponding sides.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The accepted exact native links match the tangent, circle, perpendicular-bisector and similarity steps. Only the relevant portions of the similarity-properties node are used.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower G-C.A.2, G-CO.C.9 and G-SRT.B.5 links support the actual applications. Partial links involving deriving AA from transformations or proving broader triangle theorems do not imply those tasks are completed here.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate concepts are precise and sufficient. Same-ray placement is established from the mapped geometric facts rather than assumed from an unseen diagram.
